This capstone project aims to enhance the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards (TOCCA) by developing a more secure, efficient, and user-friendly Web-Based Nomination and Voting System. This chapter presents a review of studies and systems that support the development of a

oting platform for community events like the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards (TOCCA). It carefully discusses past work about voting technologies, verification methods, user experience, system management, and accessibility to serve as the foundation for the proposed platform. The review is organized by themes to
highlight key differences, common issues, and useful ideas for the TOCCA project.
Typology and Thematic Grouping of Related Literature

The reviewed materials are organized into six main themes: (1) Voter Verification Methods, (2) Blockchain and Security Approaches, (3) User Experience in Government Services, (4) Administrative Tools and Dashboards, (5) Use of QR Codes in Participation, and (6) Local Digital Voting Examples. This structure helps explain the strengths, weaknesses, and lessons from each group, which will guide the proposed system’s design.
Sharma (2022) developed a mobile app for university elections that used One-

(OTP) authentication. This led to significant reductions in vote duplication and improved voter turnout. The approach aligns well with the TOCCA platform, which uses OTP to ensure secure, one-time voter access.

Likewise, Sreenivasa et al. (2023) proposed a more complex system incorporating Aadhaar ID, facial recognition, and voter ID. Though effective, this level of biometric integration may not be suitable for smaller-scale community systems due to privacy and infrastructure limitations.
The TOCCA platform strikes a balance by using OTP verification via mobile number, offering security while maintaining accessibility
Agrawal and Tripathi (2023) proposed a blockchain-based voting system to ensure

transparency and vote immutability. However, the complexity and resource intensity of such systems makes them impractical for community events. The TOCCA platform adopts the core principle of vote auditability by implementing secure data backups and vote logging without requiring blockchain infrastructure.

A systematic review by Civic Design (2022) emphasized the importance of intuitive design, mobile responsiveness, and multilingual support in digital civic platforms. Poor design can exclude non-technical users. The TOCCA platform addresses this by implementing a simplified interface for both mobile and desktop users, ensuring wide usability across demographics.

Civic Design (2022) noted the importance of administrative dashboards in providing real-time insights and reducing human error in vote counting and reporting. However, many systems lack exportability and customization. TOCCA incorporates real-time dashboards, automated backups, and report generation tailored for the needs of the BPLO event organizers.
5. QR Code Systems for Participation in Events

A study conducted during a Quezon City barangay festival demonstrated how QR codes at event booths enabled seamless online raffle and voting participation. This method increased participation, especially among youth. Similarly, TOCCA will use QR codes placed at business establishments to allow voters to quickly access the voting platform. These codes are secured via HTTPS links to avoid manipulation or phishing concerns.
6. Digital Voting Systems in the Philippines

The 'Pili Ka, Botante Ka' system used in Cebu for a student competition utilized centralized kiosk access but lacked mobile support and responsiveness. This limited accessibility and performance. The TOCCA system addresses these by supporting mobile access and

Mendoza and Cruz (2022) created a campus-based voting system that highlighted the feasibility of online voting. However, it lacked OTP security and had limited scalability. TOCCA builds on these findings by integrating OTP and admin-level tools tailored for public-scale use in Ormoc City.
Summary of Local and Foreign Studies and Identified Gaps

Across the reviewed literature, commonalities include the need for voter authentication, secure data handling, and mobile accessibility. Challenges identified include high costs, system complexity, limited scalability, and poor user experience. The TOCCA platform fills these gaps with a practical, community-ready solution combining secure OTP verification, QR-based access, responsive design, and real-time admin control.

Overall, this review shows that while advanced systems like blockchain and biometric scanning offers strong security, they may be too complex or costly for small community-based projects. The TOCCA system offers a more balanced and affordable option— learning from these technologies while keeping things simple and effective. It is designed to fit the needs of Ormoc City’s local community engagement.
The proposed system for the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards (TOCCA) adopts a

ased architecture to provide a secure, accessible, and efficient voting platform tailored for community-level implementation. In alignment with current technological trends, the system utilizes a combination of modern web technologies, user interface frameworks, and security tools to ensure functionality and reliability for both voters and administrators.

The frontend of the system will be developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, which are standard technologies for building responsive and interactive web applications. To enhance styling and layout responsiveness across different screen sizes, the system will use Bootstrap, a widely adopted front-end toolkit. This ensures that both desktop and mobile users experience a smooth and intuitive interface.

The backend will be powered by PHP version 8.2, a server-side scripting language known for its wide compatibility with web servers and its ability to handle dynamic content and data processing efficiently. It allows secure interaction between the application and the database, particularly for functions like vote casting, OTP generation, user validation, and admin control.

The system will use MySQL as its relational database management system. MySQL is well- suited for handling structured data and supports essential functions like data indexing, record tracking, and transaction management. It will store key information such as user identities (anonymized), votes, QR codes, categories, and system logs.

A key trend in system security today is two-factor authentication (2FA), often implemented using One-Time Passwords (OTPs). The TOCCA platform incorporates this by sending OTPs to a voter’s registered mobile number, ensuring that each vote is tied to a verified individual. This method follows best practices for enhancing voting integrity and reducing fraud.

To secure access and prevent bots or spam entries, Google reCAPTCHA or a similar CAPTCHA service may be integrated. This adds an additional layer of security during the registration or voting process.
QR codes are increasingly used in event-based applications to simplify access to digital

platforms. The proposed system will generate unique QR codes for each participating business, allowing voters to scan and be redirected to the specific voting page. This approach enhances engagement, especially for mobile users, and reduces the friction of manually entering links.
Administrators will access the system through a web-based dashboard built with the same
technologies. This dashboard will include real-time vote monitoring, category
and business management, and result exporting. Data visualization libraries such as Chart.js may be integrated to help display voting statistics clearly and interactively.

During development, the system will be hosted locally using XAMPP, which bundles Apache, PHP, and MySQL for testing purposes. For production, it may be deployed on a cloud-based or shared hosting environment with SSL support to ensure secure data transmission over HTTPS.

– Responsible for managing the event, verifying votes, updating business categories, and generating official results.

The core business activity is community-based recognition and the nomination and voting process for local businesses, organized annually through the TOCCA event. This involves:
Managing nominees under each business category
The current activity suffers from issues in verification, manual data handling, delayed reporting, and accessibility limitations. The proposed system aims to automate and simplify these operations.

At present, the voting process for the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards operates within a basic online environment, where voting links are distributed through platforms such as Facebook or messaging apps. While this allows for public participation, it lacks a centralized system that ensures voter validation, streamlined access, and real-time monitoring.
The proposed system will enhance this digital environment by introducing a web – based platform designed for structured, secure, and user-friendly participation. The platform will:
Accommodate users across desktop and mobile devices, ensuring wide accessibility regardless of device used
Provide QR code access at participating business locations to simplify voter entry and encourage on-site engagement
Offer a secure administrative dashboard for organizers, enabling real-time monitoring of votes, management of nominees, and generation of reports in an organized and efficient manner

The official nomination and voting period for the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards is conducted annually, running from June to September, in the months leading up to the awards event. This four-month window allows sufficient time for voter participation, monitoring of engagement, and processing of results. The
proposed voting platform is designed to support this timeline by offering users:
Flexible access to vote at any time within the open period using desktop or mobile devices
The ability to pause and resume voting through a draft-saving feature, enabling voters to complete their entries in multiple sessions
A real-time administrative dashboard for organizers to track participation, view live statistics, and generate accurate reports throughout the voting period.
This structured and time-sensitive system enhances the efficiency, accessibility, and transparency of the entire event process.

The research proponents will design the proposed system using a structured approach that consists of four phases: planning, analysis, design, and implementation. The planning phase will focus on identifying the scope, objectives, and beneficiaries of the system, ensuring that it meets the needs of both voters and administrators. The analysis phase will involve gathering requirements, identifying existing problems in the nomination and voting process, and modeling solutions through tools such as data flow diagrams, entity-relationship diagrams, and process flowcharts. The design phase will translate these requirements into logical and physical designs, including the database schema, user interface mockups, and system architecture aligned with usability and security standards. Finally, the implementation phase will cover coding, integration, testing, and deployment of the system using appropriate web technologies, programming languages, and database management systems, followed by validation through real-world use in the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards.

The development of the proposed system was carried out in accordance with the structured approach consisting of planning, analysis, design, and implementation. In the planning phase, the developers identified the appropriate technologies, frameworks, and standards to be used, ensuring that the system would be secure, scalable, and user-friendly. The analysis phase involved breaking down functional requirements into smaller development tasks and aligning them with industry standards such as OWASP for system security and WCAG for accessibility. The design phase focused on translating requirements into code structure, database schema, and interface layouts, following coding standards and best practices for maintainability. Finally, in the implementation phase, the system was developed using PHP, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and MySQL, integrating features such as OTP verification, QR access, and the nomination workflow, with continuous testing and debugging to ensure functionality, usability, and compliance with the requirements of the

The proponents tested the system in accordance with software development standards to ensure functionality, security, and usability. Each module was tested individually through unit testing, followed by integration testing to verify that the modules worked together correctly. The system was also subjected to user acceptance testing (UAT) by selected representatives from the BPLO and tested voters to validate that the features met the actual requirements. In addition, the BPLO, as the project client, conducted their own testing of the system to ensure that it met organizational needs and event requirements. Security and data integrity were checked following OWASP guidelines, while the interface was tested for responsiveness and accessibility on both desktop and mobile devices.

The prototype was designed as a web-based nomination and voting system that can be accessed through standard browsers on desktops and mobile devices. The system requirements include a PHP-compatible server, MySQL database, and stable internet connectivity. The preliminary design follows a modular structure, consisting of the Nomination Module, Voting Module, Administrative Dashboard, Transactions, Reports, Utilities, Archives, and Customizations. Evaluation and testing were performed by running trial events, submitting sample nominations, casting votes, and generating reports to confirm that the system flows correctly. Feedback from testers was gathered to refine the user interface, improve workflows, and fix any issues identified during the evaluation process.

The implementation of the system will follow a structured deployment plan to ensure smooth transition into an operational environment. The system will be hosted on a PHP-enabled server with MySQL database support, requiring computers with internet connectivity for administrators and mobile devices for voters. The implementation requires hardware (servers, admin computers, mobile devices), software (web server, database server, email/SMS services), facilities (internet-ready workstations), and personnel (developers, administrators, and BPLO staff). No site-specific requirements are anticipated other than stable connectivity and server access for hosting.

The implementation of the prototype produced a functional system capable of handling nominations, voting, reporting, and event management. Initial outputs include generated QR codes for establishments, nomination status reports, voter participation summaries, and category-level voting results. These outputs served as the foundation for refining the project by improving interface design, adjusting workflows for administrators, and enhancing the accuracy of reports. Feedback from testers guided revisions that made the system more user-friendly, responsive, and aligned with the needs of BPLO and the TOCCA event.

The study focused on enhancing the Tatak Ormoc Consumer’s Choice Awards (TOCCA) through the development of a Web-Based Nomination and Voting System. The system was designed and implemented to address the limitations of the previous digital process, which relied on Google Forms for nominations and a static voting platform that lacked flexibility, tracking, and administrative control. The enhanced platform now integrates modules for nominations, voting, reports, transactions, customizations, utilities, and archives, providing a more secure and organized workflow for all stakeholders. Testing confirmed that the system successfully implemented its intended features such as OTP-based verification, QR code access, draft voting with a 4-digit access code, real-time reporting, email and QR transactions, and a dynamic dashboard for monitoring. The results demonstrated improved usability, stronger data management, and better transparency for the BPLO, establishments, and voters.

The findings lead to several conclusions. The system has significantly improved the nomination process by allowing establishments to create profiles, select categories, and track their application status through a Nomination Tracker with email notifications, reducing errors and delays. The voting process was made more secure and accessible through OTP verification and QR code access, while the draft voting feature with a 4-digit access code gave voters the flexibility to pause and resume their voting progress conveniently. Administrators also benefited from enhanced tools such as real-time analytics,
reports, transaction logs, and archiving, which provided greater transparency, efficiency, and sustainability in managing the event.

Based on these conclusions, several recommendations are proposed. It is suggested that future enhancements focus on strengthening the communication features, such as providing clearer feedback messages and expanding email templates for both nominations and voting updates. The system may also benefit from additional accessibility improvements, including multilingual support or simplified layouts to further encourage voter participation. Adding a built-in helper or interactive step-by-step tutorial on the voter side

is also recommended to guide first-time users through the voting process. Finally, establishing a continuous monitoring and feedback mechanism with the BPLO and participating establishments is recommended to ensure that the system remains adaptable to the evolving needs of the event in future editions.
